title: Orchestrate presubmit fanout and add lightweight CI proxy for faster feedback
author: Asha Varma
description: Background and motivation: our presubmit lanes have grown organically and incur a large fanout of lint/test runners for every PR. This increases queue times and makes fast feedback unpredictable for small changes. This PR introduces a lightweight CI proxy (go-based) that centralizes presubmit routing decisions, performs change-aware fanout, and exposes a compact presubmit graph to downstream runners. Primary goals: (1) reduce unnecessary runner fanout for doc/style-only changes; (2) provide a single place to implement staged lanes (fast, medium, full); (3) make release hooks (signing, artifact tagging) easier to attach to an orchestration point. What this PR does: - Adds cmd/ci-proxy: a small Go binary (~600 LOC) that ingests GitHub check-run webhooks or simulated presubmit events and computes a presubmit graph based on changed paths, labels, and a new manifest (ci/presubmit-manifest.yaml). The proxy emits a compact request (route) to runner agents instead of fanout-ing to all jobs. - Introduces ci/presubmit-manifest.yaml: declarative mapping of path globs to presubmit lanes (fast/medium/full), with metadata for dependency groups and required release hooks. - Reworks GitHub workflow templates: .github/workflows/presubmit-proxy-dispatch.yml (dispatches events to the proxy) and updates to several composite actions to accept the proxy route. - Adds a lightweight Go-based runner shim (tools/runner-shim) that understands the proxy route and maps it to existing GH actions or remote executors. - Updates docs: docs/ci/README-presubmit-proxy.md and examples in redwood-quickstarts/ci-example. - Small dependency bumps in go.mod for github.com/google/go-github and sigs.k8s.io/yaml to support webhook parsing and manifest handling. Compatibility and safety: - Proxy respects existing skip conditions (ci skip, label-based skips) and defaults to conservative fanout (full) when in doubt. - No change to protected branch policies; workflow permissions unchanged. - All changes are behind the feature flag CI_PROXY_ENABLED and the proxy is disabled by default for production until rollout. Rollout plan (brief): 1) Deploy proxy in staging and run against nightly PRs for a week (no effect on real checks). 2) Enable proxy for opt-in repos/groups via a repo setting; collect telemetry (fanout reduction, queue time). 3) Flip default to enabled for small repos after 2 weeks, then expand. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for manifest parsing and route resolution - [x] Integration test harness for proxy -> runner-shim roundtrip - [x] Updated workflow templates and docs - [x] Telemetry hooks (fanout.count, presubmit.latency) - [x] Backwards-compat shim so runners that don't support proxy still receive full fanout Commits summary: - feat(ci-proxy): initial proxy command and manifest model - feat(runner-shim): implement route consumer and GH actions adapter - chore(ci): add presubmit-manifest and update workflow templates - refactor(workflows): reduce duplicated composite inputs, wire proxy route - deps(go): bump go-github and sigs.k8s.io/yaml for webhook and manifest handling - test(ci): add unit and integration tests, add test fixtures Files changed (high level): ["cmd/ci-proxy/main.go", "internal/manifest/manifest.go", "tools/runner-shim/main.go", "ci/presubmit-manifest.yaml", ".github/workflows/presubmit-proxy-dispatch.yml", ".github/workflow-templates/presubmit-template.yml", "docs/ci/README-presubmit-proxy.md", "redwood-quickstarts/ci-example/.github/workflows/ci-example.yml", "go.mod", "go.sum", "scripts/telemetry-emit.sh"]
